cases.post_rationale: The repaired query still tracks externally supplied identifiers into generic sensitive operations or authorization decisions. It contains no equality, ownership, or authenticated-session relation between requester identity and requested target user.
cases.actual_mechanism: Authorization depends on binding the requested target user identity to the authenticated session identity.

cases.post_rationale: X500Principal remains only as a generic external identity-key source. The repaired query does not model certificate class/type distinction, SCA-versus-identity certificate semantics, OIDs, or certificate-attribute validation.
cases.actual_mechanism: Authentication must distinguish the permitted identity certificate from an SCA certificate using certificate type/OID/attribute validation.

cases.post_rationale: The query retains Principal name as a generic taint source but does not model authenticated-Principal propagation or the acting-subject, organization-scope, target-object, and sensitive-operation relation.
cases.actual_mechanism: The authenticated Principal must be propagated and enforced across organization/user/API-key/password operations with the correct subject-scope-target relation.

cases.post_rationale: The repaired query still lacks the decisive relation requiring selected user identity to derive from the authenticated session identity.
cases.actual_mechanism: The selected or exposed user must derive from the authenticated session user rather than an externally supplied user identifier.

cases.post_rationale: The repaired query detects ID-like arguments reaching generic modifying operations but contains no requester-to-dashboard/message ownership or authorization relation.
cases.actual_mechanism: Dashboard/message operations require an ownership or authorization relation between requester and target resource ID.

cases.post_rationale: The repaired query contains no JDBC parameter-key filtering, sensitive-configuration validation, blacklist/allowlist, or dangerous-parameter semantics.
cases.actual_mechanism: Security-sensitive JDBC parameter keys must be filtered or replaced so dangerous parameters cannot bypass sensitive-parameter checks.

cases.post_rationale: The repaired query contains no quorum SASL peer-authentication semantics, authentication-ID instance component, server membership relation, or conditional authorization-skip logic.
cases.actual_mechanism: ZooKeeper quorum SASL authorization must not be skipped when the optional instance component of the authentication ID is absent.

interpretation: Matched V3 repair restored compilation from 0/7 to 7/7 but did not improve semantic alignment. All seven semantic labels remained unchanged. The final query still represents CWE-639 primarily as generic external identifier or Principal-derived data flowing to generic sensitive operations or authorization-decision methods. Mechanism-specific ownership, authenticated-session identity, certificate validation, JDBC sensitive-parameter filtering, SASL protocol conditions, and organization-scope relations remain absent or insufficient.
